title: Calgary officer describes life-and-death struggle with would-be robber he fatally shot
subtitle: The inquiry is being held to determine the circumstances surrounding Yacin Osman's death and whether recommendations can be made to prevent similar incidents in the future
article: When the door to Const. Ray Davies' covert vehicle suddenly swung open during an undercover operation, he thought one of his unit teammates was playing a joke on him.
But moments later Davies found himself in a life-and-death situation when a total stranger put a knife to his neck and demanded his cash.
"It was immediately apparent to me it was an attack," Davies told a Calgary fatality inquiry into the shooting death of city resident Yacin Osman.
"He put it up to my neck and face area," Davies said, of the knife Osman wielded as he opened the door to the officer's SUV.
The inquiry is being held to determine the circumstances surrounding Osman's April 9, 2018 death and whether recommendations can be made to prevent similar incidents in the future.
Davies testified he was working that night as a member of the Calgary Police Service 's strike force unit which conducts covert, undercover surveillance.
In this instance, the team was focused on a Bridgeland residence on behalf of homicide investigators.
But when Davies completed an hour of constant surveillance of the scene and was relieved by a teammate, he looked for a secluded area nearby to urinate, he told inquiry counsel Christine Nugent.
He found a location in an abandoned schoolyard and after discretely completing his business decided to check his phone messages before getting back to work.
That's when Osman, 26, yanked open the door to Davies' unmarked vehicle.
"He told me to give him all my money ... (and said) I was dead, they were going to kill me," Davies testified.
"I never in a million years thought I would get my door ripped open and a knife held to my throat."
Davies attempted to reason with Osman, but to no avail.
"I tried to negotiate with him, like, 'Hey, I'll give you everything you want,'" he said.
The officer reached around to his right hip area where he had his service weapon, hoping Osman would think he was reaching for his wallet.
"I eventually got my hand onto my gun ... Once I pull my gun out there's no turning back."
While grabbing his gun in his right hand Davies threw his left arm up in front of his face to block any knife swipes and was able to stand up outside his driver's side door.
"The fight was on and he was slashing at my face as I was blocking with my left hand," he said.
Despite his attempts to placate the would-be robber, Davies said Osman didn't show "any moment of reason."
"He didn't try to communicate with me other than to say I was dead," the officer testified.
"I thought this is life or death. He's going to kill me."
In a bid to stun his assailant, Davies twice punched Osman in the head without any reaction.
"We were inches apart. He had my shirt in one hand and he was swinging at me with the other.
"I didn't aim my gun ... I (just) pulled the trigger."
Earlier a toxicologist testified methamphetamine was found in Osman's blood.
The hearing resumes Wednesday.
